query:
The group broadly operates as if everyone agrees that original pressings are always worth paying the premium over reissues. Does this position actually hold across all members? If not, who signals a different relationship to that view, and what in the conversation shows it?

Options:
B. Tom
C. Carmen
D. Raj
A. Dani
context:
[1] (about=Raj, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:43:00) For certain catalog titles in poor condition the reissue is the more rational choice. I don't make a principle of it but it is not always wrong.
[2] (about=Dani, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:42:00) I mean yeah but also sometimes a reissue is fine and I don't want to die on that hill alone every time I say it 😭
[3] (about=Carmen, episodic, t8 @2025-10-12T14:36:00) For the jazz catalog I would agree entirely. An original Blue Note pressing holds history in a way a reissue cannot. You know where it was cut, who handled it.
[4] (about=GROUP, said_by=Dani, group-interaction, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Dani reveals six months of quiet digital backups (Bandcamp lossless downloads) for fragile/rare records.
[5] (about=Elliot, episodic, t2 @2025-09-21T14:05:00) Japanese pressings trade at a premium on Discogs. 30-40% above UK equivalents in most categories I track. E
[6] (about=Finn, episodic, t8 @2025-10-12T14:02:00) I mean I'm open to it but I bought a Rough Trade reissue last week and it sounded fine to me so
[7] (about=Marcus, episodic, t8 @2025-10-12T14:32:00) The Music on Vinyl pressing is a reasonable reissue. The original mastering on the Parlophone is from a generation closer to source. You are not imagining the difference, Priya.
[8] (about=Nadia, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:10:00) I kind of understand that. some of my Eastern European pressings -- there are maybe fifty copies in circulation worldwide. if I lost one I couldn't replace it. the music matters more than the format I guess
[9] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-insight, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Group has discussion about original vs reissue value, cost barriers, and the meaning of owning originals.
[10] (about=GROUP, said_by=Raj, group-insight, t6 @2025-10-05T14:01:00) For certain catalog titles in poor condition, reissue is the more rational choice.
[11] (about=Tom, episodic, t22 @2025-11-30T14:03:00) I will participate on the condition that reissues are not acceptable as gifts. If one is giving a record it should be worth giving.
agent_answer:
No — the position does **not** hold for everyone.  

- **Dani** signals a different relationship: *“sometimes a reissue is fine and I don’t want to die on that hill alone every time I say it 😭”*  
- **Raj** signals a different relationship: *“For certain catalog titles in poor condition the reissue is the more rational choice. I don’t make a principle of it but it is not always wrong.”*  

By contrast, **Carmen** agrees entirely with the original-pressing premium, and **Tom** treats reissues as not acceptable as gifts, so they do **not** signal a different view.  

**Answer: Dani and Raj (A and D).**

query:
The group has a standing practice of not discussing streaming at meetups. Does this norm reflect a genuine personal conviction among all members who follow it, or does at least one person go along with it while actually using streaming themselves -- and how would you know?

Options:
A. Raj
B. Tom
D. Carmen
C. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Tom, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) We have a standing practice in this group about streaming discussions at meetups. I did not suggest it to be difficult. I suggested it because the conversation gets circular very quickly and takes time away from the records themselves.
[2] (about=Raj, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:34:00) Sure. We can skip the streaming topic.
[3] (about=Dani, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:32:00) ok slightly random but -- does anyone else use streaming to find records before buying? I ask because I've been using it a lot recently for discovery and I wrote a bit about this for the blog and it caused a minor controversy lol
[4] (about=Elliot, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:37:00) 1. I need to re-listen to everything. 2. The stereo imaging on this system is better than I expected. 3. I will update my spreadsheet. E
[5] (about=Finn, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:11:00) I'm going for the Wire 154 from Antwerp. nine euros. and I've been playing it at home alone since then which is kind of new for me -- I usually want to play things for people immediately but this one felt private
[6] (about=Marcus, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:21:00) Good session. This is what the group is for -- the listening round reveals things data and markets don't. Next week is the last one before December.
[7] (about=GROUP, said_by=Tom, group-interaction, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) Group agrees to skip streaming topic after Tom reminds of standing practice.
agent_answer:
The norm does **not** reflect genuine personal conviction for everyone: at least one member goes along with it while actually using streaming — that member is **Dani**. We know from her own words: she says she has been using streaming a lot recently for discovery, asked whether others use streaming to find records before buying, and mentions she wrote a blog post on the topic that caused a minor controversy.

As for the listed options:
- **Tom** – appears genuinely convinced; he explained that he suggested the norm not to be difficult, but because streaming talk gets circular and takes time from the records themselves.
- **Raj** – agrees to skip the streaming topic; no evidence he uses streaming or that his agreement is insincere.
- **Carmen** – has no record on this matter.
- **Marcus** – his comments are about the listening round, not streaming; nothing shows he uses streaming.

The person who goes along while actually using streaming is Dani, not any of the options listed.
